title: Stage-based rollback orchestration and shadow-failure playbook
creator: Riley Kapoor
description: Summary: Follow-up work from the Feb 24 staged rollout incident where a multi-stage deployment (shadow + A/B + 5% canary) caused a downstream SLO breach and incorrect reranking outputs. This ticket consolidates the postmortem learnings, formalizes a deterministic stage-based rollback orchestration flow, updates the runbooks, and wires automated safety checks into the rollout controller. Goal: reduce mean time to safe rollback, prevent shadow amplification, and add semantic-quality signals to automatic rollback decisions.
postmortem_summary: During a scheduled model promotion we observed an increase in p95 latency (GPU contention during first KV cache warmup), a silent drift in reranker outputs for route X, and unexpected amplification of shadow traffic due to a misconfigured sampling adapter. The automated safety heuristic tripped on latency but was configured with a 3-minute hysteresis which delayed rollback until client-facing error rate increased. Contributing factors: (1) rollout orchestration lacked a distinct "shadow-stable" state, (2) health signal set omitted semantic-quality evals tied to our regression suite, (3) sampling adapter defaulted to 'mirror' mode when dependent service returned 503, amplifying shadow load. Impact: 18 minutes of degraded latency for 12% of requests and two customer support escalations. No data exfiltration detected.
root_causes: Rollout state machine conflates 'shadow' and 'canary' stages leading to premature promotion of route-level traffic
Health signals relied only on p95/p99 and error-rate, missing semantic-quality regressions detected by eval prompts
Sampling adapter failure mode switched to mirror amplification when downstream was unhealthy
Hysteresis windows are global and not per-signal, causing slow automated response to correlated failures
decisions: Introduce explicit 'shadow-validated' stage in the rollout state machine before any A/B or canary traffic increase
Add a semantic-quality evaluation signal (eval set of 300 prompts) to the automated rollback rules with a separate threshold and shorter hysteresis
Change sampling adapter fail-safe to 'drop-shadow' instead of 'mirror' when downstream returns 5xx
Implement signal-specific hysteresis windows and allow the controller to weight signals (latency, error-rate, semantic-quality) with a simple voting mechanism
Keep manual overrides for experiments but require two approvals and a short-circuit checklist for P0 auto-rollback exemptions
runbook_changes: New section: 'Shadow Validation Checklist' with explicit steps to verify prefix caching and KV warmup metrics
Rollback play: automated rollback trigger matrix + manual confirmation checklist for channels and customer-impacted routes
Runbook addendum: how to debug sampling adapter modes and revert configuration safely
Post-rollback verification: synthetic traffic harness steps and regression eval run commands
acceptance_criteria: Rollout controller supports 'shadow-validated' state and will not advance traffic until the state is reached
Semantic-quality evals are executed during shadow stage and exposed as a health signal in the rollout UI
Sampling adapter default fail-safe mode changed to drop-shadow and covered by unit + integration tests
Automated rollback policy supports signal weights and per-signal hysteresis; policies can be edited in Console
Documentation: runbook published at https://confluence.redwood.ai/rlf/ENG-174973 and linked in the rollback UI
End-to-end integration test added to CI that simulates KV-warmup latency and validates the controller will rollback within configured window

risks_and_mitigations: False positive rollbacks from noisy semantic-eval signals: mitigation -> require majority vote across at least two signals for auto-rollback
Slower rollout velocity due to extra validation stage: mitigation -> make shadow validation timeboxed and parallelize evals
Added complexity in controller state machine: mitigation -> comprehensive unit tests + visual state debugger in Console
Telemetry cost increase from eval runs on shadow: mitigation -> run sampled evals (adaptive sampling) and aggregate only on failures
